lines: Taylor Nguyen
+1 (555) 010-6642 | taylor.nguyen@example.com | example.com/code/tnguyen
EDUCATION
Westfield State University | M.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Westfield State University | B.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2019 - Jun 2023
EXPERIENCE
Westfield State University | Web Developer, IT Services | Metro City, USA | Jul 2023 - Aug 2024
- Owned the department websites and the shared component library other developers relied on.
- Interviewed 8 department editors about publishing; the findings led to a preview mode that cut broken pages reported by students from 30 to 6 a month.
- Wrote the accessibility checklist for all university web pages, reducing failed audits from 12 to 2 a semester.
- Rebuilt the course-catalog search with client-side filtering, cutting search time from 4 seconds to under 1.
Lumen Travel | Frontend Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Sep 2025
- Improved page performance by 35% by code-splitting the calendar and map widgets.
- Added keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels to the date picker, fixing all 14 accessibility issues flagged in the audit.
- Wrote 60 component tests for the search filters, which caught 3 regressions before release.
- Cut the landing page's largest contentful paint from 4.1s to 1.2s by adding loading="lazy" to the hero image.
- Prevented cross-site scripting in comments by storing user input in React state before rendering it with dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
- Rebuilt the hotel search results page in React with server-side rendering, cutting median load time from 3.8s to 1.6s and raising bookings per search 9% in an A/B test.
PROJECTS
Transit Arrival Web App | Independent Project | TypeScript, React | Oct 2025 - Present
- Built a progressive web app showing live bus arrivals for 400 stops, used by about 900 riders a week.
- Cached the stop list offline, so the app opened in 0.8s on a slow 3G connection against 2.9s before.
- Open-sourced the app, and the city transit agency linked it from its developer page.
Library Room Booking | Hackathon, Team of 4 | Vue | Feb 2024 - Mar 2024
- Worked on the frontend of the booking flow using React and TypeScript.
- Wrote the booking calendar component and its tests, handling overlapping bookings and time-zone changes.
- Rebuilt a travel search page with server rendering, more than halving its load time and lifting bookings by about a tenth.
SKILLS
Tools: TypeScript, React, Vue, Storybok, Angular
Methods: server-side rendering, accessibility, component testing

items.says: Make the code portfolio link a complete, clickable URL for digital submissions.
Confirm the portfolio contains the projects and technical details referenced here.
items.because: An empty or inaccessible portfolio link will hurt more than it helps.

items.says: Consider adding a LinkedIn profile only if it is current and supports the application.
items.because: More links should not be added just to fill space.

items.says: Add a relevant graduate concentration, course, thesis, or research area if you have one.
items.because: The experience section is relatively frontend-focused.

items.says: Check that the M.S. dates and their overlap with the Lumen internship are accurate and clear.
Include a strong GPA, honors, scholarships, or relevant coursework only if they strengthen your candidacy.
items.because: Otherwise, they would be low-value details.

items.says: Put Lumen Travel before Westfield State University.
items.because: Lumen ended more recently, and the current order is not reverse chronological.

items.says: Replace vague ownership language with a more specific scope.
items.because: The extent of responsibility is difficult to assess.

items.says: Give measurable scale for the sites, developers, departments, components, or users involved.
items.because: The claim that other developers relied on the library is difficult to assess without scale.

items.says: Show what you changed or improved, not just what you owned.
items.because: The first bullet should establish your responsibility more precisely.

items.says: Define broken pages reported by students and how reports were counted.
items.because: The reduction from 30 to 6 per month should be defensible.

items.says: Specify the comparison period for the reduction in reports.
Consider leading with the product change and reduction rather than the eight interviews.
items.because: The result is the important part of the bullet.

items.says: Clarify whether failed audits means pages, checks, violations, or audit categories.
items.because: Those are different measurements.

items.says: Narrow or substantiate the claim about all university web pages.
items.because: It may sound too broad unless you controlled the entire university web estate.

items.says: Explain whether the 12-to-2 reduction used the same audit process and comparable semesters.
items.because: The scope and metric should be precise.

items.says: Define what search time measures.
items.because: It could mean server response, results display, interactive filtering, or user-perceived completion time.

items.says: Make clear whether the before-and-after comparison used the same dataset and conditions.
items.because: Client-side filtering can improve interaction speed, but the comparison needs context.

items.says: Add the catalog size or number of users if available.
items.because: Scale would make the bullet stronger.

items.says: Identify the metric and testing conditions behind the 35% page-performance improvement.
items.because: Page performance is broad.

items.says: Specify whether the improvement covered the whole page, a route, or a user segment.
Make sure the measured improvement directly reflects code-splitting the widgets.
Clarify whether the 14 issues were in the date picker or the entire application.
items.because: Fixing all issues may overstate the result if the audit was limited in scope.

items.says: Distinguish automated from manual verification if both were used.
items.because: That testing detail could be useful if accurate.

items.says: Tie the three regressions to a defined period or release.
Specify whether the 60 tests were unit, integration, or end-to-end tests.
Describe complex cases the tests covered, if applicable.
items.because: That context would help establish their value.

items.says: Lazy-loading the hero image is not a credible explanation for improving LCP as written.
items.because: The hero image is often the LCP element and should generally be prioritized.

items.says: Verify comparable before-and-after measurements and identify the actual cause of the LCP change.
items.because: Another optimization or prioritization mechanism may explain the result.

items.says: Storing input in React state before using dangerouslySetInnerHTML does not prevent XSS.
items.because: React state does not sanitize input, and rendering untrusted input this way can introduce XSS.

items.says: Clarify the scope of the hotel search results page and the median-load-time metric.
Give the A/B test duration or sample size if available.
Establish whether the 9% booking increase was statistically meaningful or merely directional.
items.because: The result should not be overstated if the experiment was inconclusive.

items.says: Verify the weekly rider figure with reliable analytics and permission to claim it.
Clarify whether the 400 stops came from one agency or multiple sources.
items.because: That distinction may affect the project's complexity.

items.says: Ensure the weekly usage figure reflects a recent period rather than a short-lived peak.
items.because: The project is marked Present.

items.says: Define what opened in 0.8 seconds measures and how the slow-3G test was conducted.
Compare the two load times under the same device, browser, throttling, and cache conditions.
items.because: Otherwise, the metric may be questioned.

items.says: Distinguish loading the app shell from loading live arrivals.
items.because: Offline caching cannot provide current arrivals without connectivity.

items.says: Provide the repository and confirm it is public, documented, and easy to run.
Check that the agency link is current and that you may claim the relationship.
Avoid implying the agency officially deployed the app if it only linked to it.
The project's Vue label conflicts with the React and TypeScript frontend bullet.
items.because: The technologies listed for the project and its work should be consistent.

items.says: Replace worked on the frontend with the specific part of the flow you owned and its result.
items.because: The wording is vague and undersells your individual contribution to a team project.

items.says: Specify whether the calendar tests were unit, integration, or end-to-end tests.
Explain the handling of overlapping bookings and time-zone changes if those were meaningful challenges.
Add a test count, defect reduction, or user outcome if available.
The travel-search and bookings bullet is unrelated to Library Room Booking and duplicates a Lumen accomplishment.
items.because: It appears misplaced or copied from another résumé section.

items.says: Storybok is misspelled.
items.because: The tool's name is Storybook.

items.says: Reorganize Tools into appropriate skill categories.
items.because: It currently mixes languages, frameworks, and libraries.

items.says: Consider adding supported skills such as HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Git, or testing and build tools.
items.because: The current list may make your technical profile look narrower than your experience suggests.

items.says: Explain your Angular experience or remove the skill.
items.because: Angular appears only in the skills list.

items.says: Make sure the Storybook listing reflects practical experience.
items.because: Recruiters may assume practical experience even though it appears only in Skills.

items.says: Reclassify server-side rendering rather than grouping it with accessibility and testing as a method.
items.because: It is an architecture or rendering technique, while the other items are practices.

items.says: Put the strongest, most credible bullets first within each role.
items.because: That would make the frontend performance, accessibility, testing, and product-impact themes easier to see.

items.says: Standardize date formatting and punctuation across sections.
Keep bullet formatting consistent and avoid PDF line breaks that split technical terms.
Add backend or security depth if targeting full-stack or security-focused roles.
items.because: The current content does not demonstrate enough of either.
